text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov called on the ruling Socialsts to return the mandate he will hand them on Tuesday to form a new government and accept the opposition's demands for quick parliamentary elections.

-- Bulgarian students supporting the ruling Socialist party are expected to organise a protest counter-rally against the "manipulations of the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF)" in front of the UDF headquarthers in Sofia on Friday.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank raised the central interest rate to 16.5 percent monthly from 15 percent, effective from Tuesday.
-- Producer prices in Bulgaria rose 331.5 percent in December year-on-year, National Statistics Institute preliminary figures showed.

-- The ruling Bulgarian Socialist party (BSP) might withdraw its nomination of Nikolai Dobrev for prime minister if the opposition agreed to the formation of a coalition cabinet of experts with the mandate of the BSP, BSP leader Georgi Parvanov said.
-- Sofia students with faces painted in white held a "march of the dead" to protest against attempts of the Socialist party to form a new government.
-- Bulgaria's National Electricity Company (NEC) is expected to invest some 80 billion levs in power production this year, NEC officials said.
-- Bulgaria's trade unions said they would organise a human chain to block Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim on Thursday.

-- Representatives of Belgium's Solvay SA chemical company which has bought Bulgaria's soda ash producer are expected to arrive in Bulgaria to sign 30-year consession contracts for the lime and salt quarries and the thermal power plant used by Sodi, outgoing Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
